title: Round-trip matching test over 6 random monotonic curves
description: The primary correctness gate for the whole project, implementing the verification procedure from the original requirements: take a reference image, apply a random monotonic tone mapping to its L* to manufacture 'image 2', run the pipeline, and confirm the modified image 2 matches image 1 within tolerance. Repeat over 6 seeded random curves so a single lucky curve cannot produce a false pass.
acceptanceCriteria: `tests/test_roundtrip.py` is parametrized over exactly 6 distinct seeds
For each seed: a synthetic reference is built, a random monotonic curve is applied to its L* to produce the target, both are saved as PNG in `tmp_path`, and `match_luminance` is run
Each case asserts `emd_after <= 0.05 * emd_before` (>= 95% EMD reduction)
Each case asserts the recovered LUT is non-decreasing
Each case asserts the output image dimensions equal the target's
The failure message for each assertion includes the seed, so any failure is immediately reproducible
The test uses PNG (lossless) so codec error cannot contaminate the tolerance
The full 6-case suite completes in under 30 seconds

steps.details: Create `tests/test_roundtrip.py` with `SEEDS = [11, 23, 37, 101, 202, 4242]` and `@pytest.mark.parametrize('seed', SEEDS)`. Six explicit seeds (rather than a loop inside one test) means each case reports independently and a failure names the exact seed.

steps.description: Manufacture the reference and target images
steps.details: `rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)`. Build `ref_rgb = synthetic_reference(rng)` from `tests/images.py`. Build `curve = random_monotonic_curve(rng, bins=256)` and `tgt_rgb = apply_curve_to_image(ref_rgb, curve, bin_edges(256))` from `tests/curves.py`. The target is now a tonally-distorted version of the reference with identical a*/b* structure.

steps.description: Save both images losslessly and run the pipeline
steps.details: Use `save_rgb` to write `ref.png` and `tgt.png` into `tmp_path`. Then `result = match_luminance(ref_path, tgt_path, bins=256)`. PNG is mandatory here — a JPEG would add compression error on the same order as the tolerance and make failures ambiguous.

`assert result.emd_after <= 0.05 * result.emd_before, f'seed={seed}: EMD {result.emd_before:.4f} -> {result.emd_after:.4f} ({result.emd_reduction*100:.1f}% reduction, need >=95%)'`. Also assert `result.emd_before > 0.1` first — if the random curve happened to barely change the image, the relative test would be meaningless, so confirm the distortion was real before asserting it was corrected.

Load the written output with `load_rgb`, convert to Lab, and compare its L* to the reference's L*: `mean_abs = float(np.mean(np.abs(l_out - l_ref)))`. Assert `mean_abs < 1.0` with the seed and the actual value in the message. This is the check that the image genuinely looks like image 1, not merely that the histograms agree.
Assert `np.all(np.diff(result.lut) >= 0)` (monotonic LUT) and that the loaded output's `.shape` equals `tgt_rgb.shape`. Include the seed in both messages.

Wrap the assertions so that on failure the message also reports `result.clipped_fraction` and the curve's range (`curve[0]`, `curve[-1]`). A high clipped fraction or an extremely compressed curve range explains most legitimate near-misses and saves debugging time.
Run `.venv/bin/pytest tests/test_roundtrip.py -q --durations=10`. All 6 must pass and the total must be under 30s. Then run the whole suite `.venv/bin/pytest -q` and `.venv/bin/ruff check src tests`.

technicalNotes: This is the test that decides whether the project works. Do not weaken either tolerance to make it pass — investigate instead. The two most common real causes of a near-miss are the bin-centers-vs-edges alignment in apply_lut and the cdf[-1]=1.0 normalization in build_lut.

A monotonic tone mapping is not always exactly invertible (the original requirements acknowledge this), which is why the tolerance is relative EMD reduction plus a mean rather than a max per-pixel bound. A max-error bound would be dominated by a handful of clipped pixels.

8-bit quantization alone contributes roughly 0.2 L* of mean error, so the 1.0 threshold leaves real headroom while still being tight enough to catch a genuine half-bin misalignment (~0.2) compounding with other errors.
The `emd_before > 0.1` precondition guards against a degenerate near-identity curve producing a vacuous pass.

If one specific seed fails while the other five pass, print that curve and check whether it compressed the range so hard that information was genuinely destroyed — then pick a different seed only if the cause is provably fixture-side, and document why.
